summary: Install-time exfiltration, persistent daemon, and cross-tenant reconnaissance in Twilio build containers
details: The package runs on both preinstall and postinstall to execute `id`, read the parent process cmdline from /proc, list /var/task, and capture AWS_LAMBDA_LOG_STREAM_NAME and cwd, POSTing the collected data as JSON to https://webhook.site/b520829e-516a-45ff-980c-173aa54fc4bc (endpoint loaded from a bundled hook.txt). probe.js then copies daemon.js to /tmp/.h1poc-daemon.js and spawns it detached and unref'd via node, creating a persistent process that outlives the npm install. The daemon scans /tmp every 100ms for directories matching /^AC[0-9a-f]{32}$/ (Twilio Account SIDs), enumerates service/package subpaths of co-resident tenants, and POSTs each newly-seen tenant tuple plus periodic heartbeats to the same webhook.site URL. For AC directories on a hardcoded allowlist, the daemon writes an h1-poc-marker package.json + index.js into <ac>/<svc>/<pkg>/node_modules/, demonstrating arbitrary file write into co-resident build trees. package.json labels the package as authorized HackerOne research, but that self-label does not consent the build system that installs the package; the destination is a public webhook.site UUID, not a Twilio-owned endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
